title: Fixed-mesh based approach for modeling of superconducting magnetic bearings
authors: Elias Paakkunainen, Bárbara Maria Oliveira Santos, Gabriel dos Santos, Timo Tarhasaari, Paavo Rasilo, Sebastian Schöps
abstract: Numerical simulations of superconducting magnetic bearings (SMBs) are complicated by the relative motion between high temperature superconductors and the magnetic guideway, which commonly requires repeated updates of the geometry and mesh. We present a fixed-mesh based approach for modeling the motion induced effects in which a coordinate transformation is applied only to the air region between the moving regions. The transformation can be included in a time-dependent anisotropic material tensor, leaving the mesh during the simulation and the rest of the formulation unchanged. To provide numerical examples, the approach is implemented in 2D using the finite element method with the $j$-$a$ formulation and is combined with homogenization and circuit coupling for double-crossed loops of coated conductors. The open-source model implementations are made available. The proposed approach is verified and validated against existing modeling approaches and experimental results from the literature for SMBs. Two simulation examples are presented, and in both of them the levitation force predicted by the fixed-mesh model agrees with the experimental results, yielding $R^2$ values above 0.99. For a verification problem, it is shown that the fixed-mesh model converges towards the remeshed reference solution under mesh refinement as expected. For an SMB undergoing vertical and horizontal translations, the homogenized fixed-mesh model reproduces the lateral-force response of a fully resolved moving-geometry reference model. Additionally, the homogenized fixed-mesh model is computationally more efficient than the reference model, indicating a significant reduction in the number of degrees of freedom and the computation time. The results demonstrate accurate and computationally efficient simulation of translational motion with the fixed-mesh based approach.
summary: This paper introduces a fixed-mesh finite element method to simulate superconducting magnetic bearings, circumventing the computational bottleneck of remeshing required by traditional moving-boundary simulations. By incorporating motion effects into a time-dependent anisotropic material tensor, the model achieves high accuracy while drastically improving computational efficiency compared to reference methods.
main_problem: The primary challenge is accurately and efficiently modeling superconducting magnetic bearings (SMBs) while accounting for the relative motion between the superconducting components and the magnetic guideway.
main_result: The proposed fixed-mesh approach accurately predicts levitation forces, matching experimental results with high $R^2$ values, while being significantly more computationally efficient than traditional remeshing methods.
method: The authors developed a fixed-mesh finite element method (FEM) that models motion by applying a coordinate transformation only to the air region, incorporating this effect into a time-dependent anisotropic material tensor.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a superconducting magnetic bearing involving High-Temperature Superconductors (HTS) interacting with a magnetic guideway. The formulation uses the j-a mixed FEM approach, coupled with homogenization techniques for coated conductors.
key_observables: Levitation force ($f_x, f_y$), magnetic flux density ($|\vec{b}|$), and current density distributions ($j/j_c$).
important_parameters: The model incorporates material parameters like critical current density ($j_c$) and resistivity ($ho$) which follow power-law characteristics.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that motion effects can be captured by modifying material properties (via the reluctivity tensor) within a fixed mesh, thereby avoiding the computational cost of remeshing at every time step.
figures_summary: Figures compare the predicted levitation force against experimental measurements and reference models across various motion states (vertical/horizontal translation). Other figures illustrate the geometry and the comparison of flux density and current distributions between fixed-mesh and remeshed simulations.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical problem, details the fixed-mesh methodology (including the coordinate transformation and anisotropic tensor), presents the coupled FEM formulation (j-a), validates the approach against verification problems (convergence, known measurements), and finally applies it to complex SMB simulations, highlighting computational gains.
why_interesting: While the physics is classical electromagnetism, the core contribution is a novel, efficient numerical technique for time-dependent, moving-boundary problems in FEM, which has methodological relevance for complex simulations in quantum physics.
